Q4_K x Q8_1 x4 dense prompt probe preserving the accepted BM128/BN128/WG256/WAVE64/TM4/TN2 schedule while increasing staged K blocks from BK_STEP=1 to BK_STEP=2. This directly tests the Vulkan oracle staging-depth/resource delta: RADV uses 22528 bytes LDS and 192 VGPR without spills, while the accepted HRX route uses 8192 bytes LDS and 139 VGPR. The probe compiled through CMake/Ninja with 16384 bytes LDS, 145 VGPR, and no spills, and passed p512 plus p513/p33 focused correctness, but mixed p512 gains did not hold on p513 tail rows. Keep it opt-in only as a bounded staging-depth diagnostic.

Packed-Q8_1/x4 B-cache ownership probe after direct-F32 WMMA clones, narrower output ownership, and row padding failed. It preserves the accepted Q4_K MMQL128 production dataflow, BM128, BN128, wave64, BK_STEP1, and output ownership, but changes staged B payload ownership from two lanes per row loading four packed words each to four lanes per row loading two packed words each. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=48, VGPR=140, LDS=8192, no spills, 512 static v_dot sites, 46 ds_loads, 12 ds_stores, 18 global loads, 64 global stores, 188 s_waitcnts, and 2 barriers. The route selected correctly for p512 and p513, passed focused CPU-reference rows for p512 and p513, and kept exact p33 on the existing MMQ64 route. It is rejected for production promotion because same-runner p513 focused perf regressed on every row, and p512 only produced small FFN gains while regressing K/Q rows. Keep it opt-in only as a bounded load-ownership diagnostic.

Packed-Q8_1/x4 LDS-read issue-order probe after direct-F32 WMMA clones, cache padding, B payload split, and narrower output ownership failed. It preserves the current Q4_K MMQL128 production dataflow, BM128, BN128, wave64, BK_STEP1, and output ownership, but preloads the two B-cache rows for each TN=2 micro-iteration before issuing dots. This brackets the Vulkan oracle's large LDS-read window and gradual wait-drain pattern while staying in the current packed-Q8_1 path. It is opt-in and guarded to full column tiles only because exact p513 tail timing was mixed/regressive before the guard. Focused p512/p33/p513 correctness passed after the guard, p512 selected bpair, p513 fell back to current MMQL128, and p33 stayed on narrow routes. DeepSeek Q4_K_M p512/fa1 same-binary model A/B improved 246.34 -> 258.77 tok/s.

evidence_summary.selection: Packed-Q8_1/x4 LDS-read issue-order probe following the positive full-tile B-pair result. It preserves the current Q4_K MMQL128 production dataflow, BM128, BN128, wave64, BK_STEP1, and output ownership, but preloads four B-cache rows across two adjacent WNITER positions before issuing dots. This moves one step closer to RADV's broad post-barrier LDS-read window. It compiles through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=53, VGPR=169, LDS=8192, no spills. Focused p512/p33/p513 correctness passed; p512 selected B-quad, p33 stayed narrow, and the p513 large-tail policy selected B-quad by default with rollback to current MMQL128. Same-binary model A/B improved DeepSeek Q4_K_M p512/fa1 249.47 -> 261.03 tok/s, Llama 3.1 8B Q4_K_M p512/fa1 499.38 -> 527.82 tok/s, and Llama 3.1 8B Q4_K_M p513/fa1 564.62 -> 585.20 tok/s. It is default on gfx1151 only, with rollback GGML_HRX_DISABLE_Q4_K_Q8_1_X4_MMQL128_BQUAD_PROMPT=1 for all B-quad and GGML_HRX_DISABLE_Q4_K_Q8_1_X4_MMQL128_BQUAD_TAIL_PROMPT=1 for large tails.

Packed-Q8_1/x4 output-ownership probe after direct-F32 WMMA clones failed. It keeps the Q4_K MMQL staged packed dataflow, BM128, wave64, and BK_STEP1, but narrows the column tile to BN64/WN32 so each lane holds half the current MMQL128x128 accumulator footprint. It tests whether current MMQL128 is limited by live output state rather than packed A/B reuse. Opt-in only; p33 remains on the narrow route unless separately proven.

Packed-Q8_1/x4 LDS-resource probe after direct-F32 WMMA clones and lower-column ownership failed. It preserves the current Q4_K MMQL128 dataflow, BM128, BN128, wave64, and BK_STEP1, but pads the shared A cache rows from 24 to 32 bytes and packed-B cache rows from 40 to 64 bytes. This tests whether the Vulkan oracle's larger padded LDS footprint and load/wait behavior are the missing axis while keeping p33 on the existing narrow route unless separately proven.

Direct-F32 Q4_K staged WMMA probe anchored to the Vulkan oracle matmul_q4_k_f32_f16acc_aligned_l schedule. RADV emits v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16 with 22528 bytes LDS and no spills, while the current HRX Q4 MMQL128 route emits integer v_dot4_i32_iu8. This probe stages a 64x32 by 16 f16 A/B panel in LDS to test the opcode/dataflow axis before attempting a full 128x128 Vulkan clone.

Vulkan-large direct-F32 Q4_K WMMA probe anchored to matmul_q4_k_f32_f16acc_aligned_l. The oracle uses BM128/BN128/BK32/WG256, LOAD_VEC_A=4, LOAD_VEC_B=8, Q4_K dequant to f16 LDS, F32 RHS conversion to f16 LDS, and v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16 with 22528 bytes LDS. This HIP probe keeps the same 128x128/BK32/direct-RHS class and multiple 16x16 WMMA accumulator tiles per workgroup. It is opt-in only until focused p512/p513 correctness and timing beat the current MMQL128 route; p33 must remain on the existing narrow route unless separately proven.

Single-axis follow-up to the rejected VK128 direct-F32 Q4_K WMMA probe. It keeps BM128/BN128/BK32/WG256 and direct F32 RHS, but changes the A/B shared row stride from 32 halfs to Vulkan's padded 40-half f16vec2-equivalent stride from mul_mm.comp (SHMEM_STRIDE=20 f16vec2). This isolates LDS padding/bank behavior while preserving route policy: opt-in only, p33 remains on the narrow route, and p512/p513 must beat current MMQL128 before promotion.

Single-axis follow-up to the rejected VK128 padded direct-F32 Q4_K WMMA probe. It preserves BM128/BN128/BK32/WG256, direct F32 RHS, and Vulkan's 40-half padded LDS stride, but explicitly prefetches both k-half A/B LDS fragments for each output tile before issuing WMMA. This moves the HIP lowering toward RADV's deeper LDS-load-before-WMMA cadence while staying wave32 because the ROCm WMMA builtin rejects wave64 compilation.

Exact-schedule follow-up to the rejected VK128 padded direct-F32 Q4_K WMMA probes. It preserves BM128/BN128/BK32/WG256, direct F32 RHS, and Vulkan's 40-half padded LDS stride, but remaps pairs of wave32 waves to one Vulkan-style 64x64 output owner. This tests the RADV subgroup-64 ownership axis while staying within the HIP WMMA builtin's wave32 compile requirement.

Exact-schedule follow-up to the rejected VK128 padded direct-F32 Q4_K WMMA probes. It uses the ROCm wave64 WMMA builtin, Vulkan's BM128/BN128/BK32/WG256 tile, the 40-half padded LDS stride, and the RDNA3 matrix-calculator A/B/D fragment mapping for v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16 wave64.

OPSEL high-half diagnostic for the wave64 VK128 padded direct-F32 Q4_K WMMA route. It uses the ROCm wave64 WMMA builtin and the RDNA3 matrix-calculator fragment mapping, but selects the high accumulator half after the low-half route failed focused correctness with finite error.

RADV-ISA-driven follow-up to the rejected wave64 VK128 padded direct-F32 Q4_K WMMA route. It preserves BM128/BN128/BK32/WG256, direct F32 RHS, Vulkan's 40-half padded LDS stride, the ROCm wave64 WMMA builtin, and the same OPSEL/store policy, but spells LDS fragment reads as half4 chunks to target the RADV b64-style LDS feed rather than the existing HIP route's coalesced ds_load_b128 fragment loads. It is rejected at the compile/ISA gate: non-volatile half4 source coalesced back to the existing ds_load_b128 pattern (32 ds_load_b128, 0 ds_load_b64, 32 WMMA, 155 waits, SGPR=29, VGPR=165, LDS=20480), while a volatile spelling emitted flat_load_b64 with immediate vmcnt waits, raised VGPR to 233, and dropped to 28 static WMMA sites. Keep it opt-in only as evidence that C++ half4 source spelling is not enough to recover RADV's ds_load_b64 schedule.

RADV-ISA-driven follow-up to the rejected wave64 VK128 padded half4 source probe. It preserves BM128/BN128/BK32/WG256, direct F32 RHS, Vulkan's 40-half padded LDS stride, the ROCm wave64 WMMA builtin, and the same OPSEL/store policy, but uses explicit ds_read_b64 inline assembly for A/B LDS fragment reads. It is rejected after focused correctness: the route emitted LDS ds_load_b64 and selected correctly for p512/p513 while p33 stayed on the narrow route, but p512 and p513 CPU-reference rows failed. Adding a memory clobber to the inline read changed the failure from NaN/inf to finite ERR around 0.006-0.012 on p512 and 0.0016-0.0118 on p513, proving optimizer visibility matters, but direct half4 asm output, conservative s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0) after each read, and explicit address_space(3) base-pointer arithmetic still did not pass correctness. The final emitted schedule has 256 ds_load_b64, 0 ds_load_b128, 32 WMMA, 396 waits, SGPR=30, VGPR=169, LDS=20480. Keep it opt-in only as evidence that forced ds_load_b64 is possible, but this fragment spelling is not semantically equivalent to the RADV schedule.

RADV-ISA-driven follow-up to the rejected wave64 VK128 padded B64ASM diagnostic. It preserves BM128/BN128/BK32/WG256, direct F32 RHS, Vulkan's 40-half padded LDS stride, the ROCm wave64 WMMA builtin, OPSEL/store policy, and explicit ds_read_b64 LDS fragment reads, but changes the compute window to load four A fragments and four B fragments for each k-half, wait, then issue the 4x4 WMMA block. The no-wait grouping emitted the target 64 ds_load_b64 / 32 WMMA shape but failed focused p512/p513 correctness with NaNs. The conservative waited grouping still emitted 64 ds_load_b64, 0 ds_load_b128, 32 WMMA, 206 waits, SGPR=29, VGPR=199, LDS=20480, no spills, and passed focused p512, p33, and p513 CPU-reference gates while selecting only p512/p513. It is rejected for production promotion because same-row Kcur p512 perf regressed badly versus current MMQL128: 1038.69 us -> 3103.19 us. Keep it opt-in as evidence that matching RADV's LDS load count and fragment reuse is not sufficient while the HIP inline-asm wait schedule remains far from RADV.

Q5_K packed-Q8_1/x4 follow-up to the positive Q4_K B-quad schedule axis. It preserves the current Q5 MMQL128 packed dataflow, BM128, BN128, wave64, and BK_STEP1 while preloading four B-cache rows across two adjacent WNITER positions before dot consumption. It compiled without spills and passed focused p512, p33, and p513 CPU-reference gates with the intended full-tile selector policy, but regressed same-runner p512 focused timing on all four Q5 rows. Keep opt-in only as negative transfer evidence; do not promote.
